comparisons.peer_summary: The company operates through four business segments: Consumer Banking, Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM), Global Banking, and Global Markets, with remaining operations recorded in All Other.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures detail the organizational structure of their wealth and investment management divisions, though GS frames this within a specific 'Sustainable Finance' context while BAC describes the broader operational segments. GS explicitly notes that its Asset & Wealth Management division provides 'sustainability-related capabilities... across public and private markets' and utilizes 'specialist sustainability teams,' whereas BAC identifies 'Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM)' as one of its four primary business segments providing a 'diversified range of banking and nonbank financial services' without specifying sustainability specialization in this segment summary.

sentences.text: Within Asset & Wealth Management, we provide clients sustainability-related capabilities, across public and private markets and open architecture, proprietary and third-party products, portfolio strategy and implementation, and specialist sustainability teams and strategies.

comparisons.peer_summary: Effective in Q2 2024, JPMorganChase combined its former Corporate & Investment Bank and Commercial Banking segments to form the Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB), resulting in three reportable segments: Consumer & Community Banking (CCB), CIB, and Asset & Wealth Management (AWM), with remaining activities in Corporate.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures outline the firm's business segment structure, with GS identifying 'Asset & Wealth Management' as a component of its strategy, while JPMorganChase lists 'Asset & Wealth Management (AWM)' as one of its three reportable business segments. The texts are comparable in describing the firm's organizational breakdown, but GS's disclosure focuses on the sustainability-specific services within that arm, whereas JPMorgan's disclosure focuses on the corporate reorganization and formation of the Commercial & Investment Bank (CIB).
